```{r setup, include = FALSE}
library(nlmixr2lib)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Dorofaeff_2026_piperacillin_tazobactam"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Dorofaeff_2026_piperacillin_tazobactam"))$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1128/aac.00272-26>

```{r model}
mod <- readModelDb("Dorofaeff_2026_piperacillin_tazobactam")
ui <- rxode2::rxode(mod)
th <- ui$theta
```

Piperacillin and tazobactam are given together in a fixed 8:1 ratio
(100/12.5 mg/kg). The model gives each drug its own one-compartment,
first-order-elimination disposition. The two drugs were fitted jointly, with
correlated between-subject variability, but they do not interact.
Piperacillin uses the unsuffixed canonical names and tazobactam carries the
`_taz` sibling-drug suffix.

```{r constants}
# Clinical and target-attainment constants, all from the source paper.
PIP_MGKG <- 100 # piperacillin dose (mg/kg), maximum 4 g per dose
TAZ_MGKG <- 12.5 # tazobactam dose (mg/kg), maximum 0.5 g per dose
TAU <- 6 # dosing interval (h)
FU <- 0.70 # unbound fraction: Methods assume 30% protein binding
CT_TAZ <- 2 # tazobactam threshold (mg/L), target 85% fT > 2 mg/L
MICS <- c(1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64) # piperacillin MIC range (mg/L)
```

# Population

Thirty-one critically ill children (11 infants aged 1 month to < 1 year and 20
children up to 12 years) were studied in the paediatric intensive care unit of
Queensland Children's Hospital, Brisbane, between June 2019 and February 2023
(Table 1). Median age was 1.8 years (range 0.1-11.8), median weight 10.80 kg
(range 3-68) and 17/31 (54.8%) were female. Median PELOD-2 score was 5; 61.3%
were mechanically ventilated and 38.7% received vasopressors or inotropes.
Median Schwartz eGFR was 120.5 mL/min/1.73 m^2 (range 54.3-289) and 44.8% of
the patients with an eGFR had augmented renal clearance (eGFR > 130).

Piperacillin-tazobactam 100/12.5 mg/kg (maximum 4 g piperacillin) was given
every 6 h as a 30-min infusion. Samples were taken before a dose and 60, 120,
240 and 360 min after the start of the infusion: 102 piperacillin and 97
tazobactam total plasma concentrations in all.

The same information is available from the model's `population` metadata
(`readModelDb("Dorofaeff_2026_piperacillin_tazobactam")()$population`).

# Event-table helpers

```{r helpers}
# Doses go to the real ODE states (central, central_taz). Observation rows use
# dvid = 1 with no cmt, which is the form that works for a two-endpoint rxUi.
dose_rows <- function(regimen, pip_mg, taz_mg, n_doses) {
  if (regimen == "Continuous infusion") {
    total_h <- n_doses * TAU
    return(data.frame(
      time = c(0, 0), evid = 1L, cmt = c("central", "central_taz"),
      amt = c(pip_mg, taz_mg) * n_doses,
      rate = c(pip_mg, taz_mg) * n_doses / total_h, dvid = NA_integer_
    ))
  }
  dur <- switch(regimen,
    "0.5-h infusion every 6 h" = 0.5,
    "3-h infusion every 6 h" = 3,
    stop("unknown regimen: ", regimen)
  )
  t <- rep(seq(0, by = TAU, length.out = n_doses), each = 2)
  data.frame(
    time = t, evid = 1L, cmt = rep(c("central", "central_taz"), n_doses),
    amt = rep(c(pip_mg, taz_mg), n_doses),
    rate = rep(c(pip_mg, taz_mg) / dur, n_doses), dvid = NA_integer_
  )
}

obs_rows <- function(grid) {
  data.frame(
    time = grid, evid = 0L, cmt = NA_character_, amt = NA_real_,
    rate = NA_real_, dvid = 1L
  )
}

# One event block per subject; `subjects` has id, WT, AGE, CRCL, regimen.
make_events <- function(subjects, n_doses, grid) {
  bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(subjects)), function(i) {
    s <- subjects[i, , drop = FALSE]
    pip_mg <- min(PIP_MGKG * s$WT, 4000)
    taz_mg <- min(TAZ_MGKG * s$WT, 500)
    ev <- bind_rows(dose_rows(s$regimen, pip_mg, taz_mg, n_doses), obs_rows(grid))
    cbind(s[rep(1, nrow(ev)), , drop = FALSE], ev)
  })) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
}

N_DOSES <- 16 # 96 h of dosing; the last 6-h interval (90-96 h) is at steady state
SS_GRID <- seq(90, 96, by = 0.05)
```

# Virtual cohort

Individual covariates are not published. The cohort below takes its age
strata from Table 1 (35.5% aged 1 month to < 1 year, 25.8% 1 to < 4 years,
19.4% 4 to < 9 years and 19.4% 9 to < 12 years). Weight comes from the WHO
weight-for-age medians (sexes averaged), with log-normal scatter; this is
external reference data, used only to build a plausible covariate
distribution. eGFR is log-normal around the Table 1 median of 120.5
mL/min/1.73 m^2, truncated to the observed range 54.3-289.

```{r cohort}
# WHO weight-for-age median (kg) by age (months), sexes averaged. External
# reference data (WHO Child Growth Standards 0-5 y; WHO Growth Reference 5-19 y).
who_age_mo <- c(0, 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 12, 18, 24, 36, 48, 60, 72, 84, 96, 108, 120, 132, 144)
who_wt_kg <- c(
  3.3, 4.4, 5.5, 6.3, 7.8, 8.8, 9.5, 10.8, 12.0, 14.2, 16.2,
  18.3, 20.5, 22.9, 25.6, 28.6, 32.0, 35.9, 40.1
)

draw_egfr <- function(n) {
  out <- numeric(0)
  while (length(out) < n) {
    y <- rlnorm(3 * n, meanlog = log(120.5), sdlog = 0.4)
    out <- c(out, y[y >= 54.3 & y <= 289])
  }
  out[seq_len(n)]
}

set.seed(20261018)
N_COHORT <- 200
stratum <- sample(1:4, N_COHORT, replace = TRUE, prob = c(11, 8, 6, 6))
lo <- c(1 / 12, 1, 4, 9)[stratum]
hi <- c(1, 4, 9, 12)[stratum]
cohort <- data.frame(
  id = seq_len(N_COHORT),
  AGE = runif(N_COHORT, lo, hi),
  CRCL = draw_egfr(N_COHORT),
  regimen = "0.5-h infusion every 6 h"
) |>
  mutate(WT = stats::approx(who_age_mo, who_wt_kg, xout = 12 * AGE, rule = 2)$y *
    exp(rnorm(N_COHORT, 0, 0.15)))

cohort |>
  summarise(
    `Median age (y)` = median(AGE), `Median weight (kg)` = median(WT),
    `Median eGFR` = median(CRCL), `% eGFR > 130` = 100 * mean(CRCL > 130)
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Virtual cohort (Table 1: median age 1.8 y, weight 10.80 kg, eGFR 120.5, 44.8% > 130).")

stopifnot(
  abs(median(cohort$AGE) - 1.8) < 1.5,
  abs(median(cohort$WT) - 10.8) < 4,
  abs(median(cohort$CRCL) - 120.5) < 20
)
```

# Visual predictive check (Figure 2)

The study sampled one dosing interval of an ongoing q6h regimen, so the cohort
is simulated to steady state and the last interval is plotted against time
after the dose. The observed medians in the table are read by the maintainers
from Figure 2 at the nominal sampling times.

```{r vpc}
vpc_events <- make_events(cohort, N_DOSES, seq(90, 96, by = 0.1))
vpc <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod,
  events = vpc_events, useLinCmt = FALSE,
  returnType = "data.frame"
) |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  mutate(tad = time - 90)

vpc_long <- vpc |>
  select(id, tad, Cc, Cc_taz) |>
  pivot_longer(c(Cc, Cc_taz), names_to = "analyte", values_to = "conc") |>
  mutate(analyte = ifelse(analyte == "Cc", "Piperacillin", "Tazobactam"))

vpc_sum <- vpc_long |>
  group_by(analyte, tad) |>
  summarise(
    p05 = quantile(conc, 0.05), p50 = median(conc), p95 = quantile(conc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(vpc_sum, aes(tad)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p05, ymax = p95), alpha = 0.25, fill = "steelblue") +
  geom_line(aes(y = p50), colour = "steelblue4") +
  facet_wrap(~analyte, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    x = "Time after last dose (h)", y = "Total plasma concentration (mg/L)",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 2 of Dorofaeff 2026 (typical 5th-50th-95th percentiles, no residual error)."
  )
```

```{r vpc-compare}
fig2_obs <- data.frame(
  analyte = rep(c("Piperacillin", "Tazobactam"), each = 4),
  tad = rep(c(1, 2, 4, 6), 2),
  observed_median = c(172, 70, 25, 13, 20, 11, 4.6, 3)
)
vpc_cmp <- vpc_sum |>
  filter(abs(tad - round(tad)) < 1e-6, round(tad) %in% c(1, 2, 4, 6)) |>
  mutate(tad = round(tad)) |>
  inner_join(fig2_obs, by = c("analyte", "tad")) |>
  mutate(ratio = p50 / observed_median)

vpc_cmp |>
  select(analyte, tad, observed_median, p50, ratio) |>
  rename(
    Analyte = analyte, `Time after dose (h)` = tad,
    `Figure 2 observed median (mg/L)` = observed_median,
    `Simulated median (mg/L)` = p50, `Simulated / observed` = ratio
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2)

# Figure 2 medians come from 31 patients with a different covariate mix, so
# the check is on the centre of the ratios, not on any single time point.
stopifnot(
  nrow(vpc_cmp) == 8,
  abs(log(median(vpc_cmp$ratio))) < log(1.5)
)
```

# Probability of target attainment (Figure 3)

Figure 3 simulates a 2-year-old child of 11 kg at eGFR 80, 120 and 160
mL/min/1.73 m^2, given piperacillin 100 mg/kg with tazobactam 12.5 mg/kg every
6 h as a 0.5-h or 3-h infusion, or the same daily dose as a continuous
infusion. Unbound concentrations are 70% of total. A subject attains the
piperacillin target when the unbound concentration stays above the MIC for the
whole dosing interval, and the tazobactam target when the unbound concentration
exceeds 2 mg/L for at least 85% of it. Both are scored over the steady-state
interval 90-96 h. The paper used 1,000 subjects per scenario; 200 are used here.

```{r pta-sim}
regimens <- c("0.5-h infusion every 6 h", "3-h infusion every 6 h", "Continuous infusion")
N_PER_ARM <- 200
pta_subjects <- expand.grid(
  rep = seq_len(N_PER_ARM), CRCL = c(80, 120, 160), regimen = regimens,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
) |>
  mutate(id = row_number(), WT = 11, AGE = 2) |>
  select(id, WT, AGE, CRCL, regimen)

pta_events <- make_events(pta_subjects, N_DOSES, SS_GRID)
pta_sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod,
  events = pta_events, keep = "regimen",
  useLinCmt = FALSE, returnType = "data.frame"
) |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  select(id, time, CRCL, regimen, Cc, Cc_taz, cl, cl_taz)

per_subject <- pta_sim |>
  group_by(id, CRCL, regimen) |>
  summarise(
    fmin_pip = min(FU * Cc),
    taz_frac = mean(FU * Cc_taz > CT_TAZ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

pta <- bind_rows(lapply(MICS, function(m) {
  per_subject |>
    group_by(CRCL, regimen) |>
    summarise(
      Piperacillin = 100 * mean(fmin_pip > m),
      Combined = 100 * mean(fmin_pip > m & taz_frac >= 0.85),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    mutate(MIC = m)
})) |>
  pivot_longer(c(Piperacillin, Combined), names_to = "panel", values_to = "simulated")
```


```{r fig3-assert}
pta_cmp |>
  group_by(panel, regimen) |>
  summarise(
    `Median |difference| (points)` = median(abs(diff)),
    `Max |difference| (points)` = max(abs(diff)), .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  rename(Panel = panel, Regimen = regimen) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)

# 200 subjects per arm give a Monte Carlo standard error of up to 3.5 points
# per cell, and the published values are read off a figure, so the gate is on
# the centre and a robust upper quantile of the 126 differences.
stopifnot(
  median(abs(pta_cmp$diff)) < 3,
  quantile(abs(pta_cmp$diff), 0.9) < 10
)
```

## Continuous infusion in closed form

Under continuous infusion the steady-state concentration is the infusion rate
divided by clearance, so the piperacillin PTA has a closed form:
`P(FU * R / CL > MIC) = pnorm(log(FU * R / (MIC * CL_typ)) / omega_CL)`. This
removes Monte Carlo error and tests the clearance model directly, including the
eGFR exponent. Table 2 gives 0.65 for that exponent and the display equation
prints 0.76; both are scored against Figure 3 at the MICs where the PTA is not
at a floor or ceiling.

```{r ci-closed-form}
rate_pip <- PIP_MGKG * 11 / TAU # mg/h for the 11-kg child
omega_cl <- sqrt(ui$omega["etalcl", "etalcl"])
cl_typ <- function(egfr, e_crcl) {
  exp(th[["lcl"]]) * (11 / 70)^0.75 * (egfr / 117.9)^e_crcl * (2 / 1.8)^th[["e_age_cl"]]
}
ci_cf <- expand.grid(CRCL = c(80, 120, 160), MIC = c(32, 64)) |>
  mutate(
    `Table 2 (0.65)` = 100 * pnorm(log(FU * rate_pip / (MIC * cl_typ(CRCL, 0.65))) / omega_cl),
    `Equation (0.76)` = 100 * pnorm(log(FU * rate_pip / (MIC * cl_typ(CRCL, 0.76))) / omega_cl)
  ) |>
  inner_join(
    fig3 |> filter(panel == "Piperacillin", regimen == "Continuous infusion"),
    by = c("CRCL", "MIC")
  ) |>
  select(CRCL, MIC, published, `Table 2 (0.65)`, `Equation (0.76)`)

ci_cf |>
  rename(eGFR = CRCL, `MIC (mg/L)` = MIC, `Figure 3 (%)` = published) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1)

rmse <- function(x) sqrt(mean((x - ci_cf$published)^2))
c(table2 = rmse(ci_cf$`Table 2 (0.65)`), equation = rmse(ci_cf$`Equation (0.76)`))

# Closed form against the published figure: the packaged exponent must fit
# Figure 3 better than the display equation's.
stopifnot(rmse(ci_cf$`Table 2 (0.65)`) < rmse(ci_cf$`Equation (0.76)`))
```

# NCA with PKNCA

PKNCA is run on the steady-state interval (90-96 h) of the eGFR 120 arms of
the Figure 3 simulation, for each drug and regimen. Dorofaeff 2026 reports no
NCA, so the check is internal: at steady state the AUC over one interval must
equal the dose per interval divided by the subject's clearance.

```{r pknca}
nca_in <- pta_sim |>
  filter(CRCL == 120) |>
  select(id, time, regimen, Cc, Cc_taz, cl, cl_taz)

run_nca <- function(conc_col, label, dose_mg) {
  dose_ss <- nca_in |>
    distinct(id, regimen) |>
    mutate(time = 90, amt = dose_mg)
  conc <- nca_in |>
    filter(!is.na(.data[[conc_col]])) |>
    mutate(conc = .data[[conc_col]])
  conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc, conc ~ time | regimen + id, concu = "mg/L", timeu = "h")
  dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_ss, amt ~ time | regimen + id, doseu = "mg")
  intervals <- data.frame(
    start = 90, end = 96, cmax = TRUE, cmin = TRUE, auclast = TRUE, cav = TRUE
  )
  res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
  as.data.frame(res$result) |> mutate(analyte = label)
}

nca_res <- bind_rows(
  run_nca("Cc", "Piperacillin", PIP_MGKG * 11),
  run_nca("Cc_taz", "Tazobactam", TAZ_MGKG * 11)
)

nca_res |>
  group_by(analyte, regimen, PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(median = median(PPORRES), .groups = "drop") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = median) |>
  rename(
    Analyte = analyte, Regimen = regimen, `Cmax,ss (mg/L)` = cmax,
    `Cmin,ss (mg/L)` = cmin, `AUC0-6,ss (mg*h/L)` = auclast, `Cavg,ss (mg/L)` = cav
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Median steady-state NCA, 2-year-old 11-kg child, eGFR 120.")

auc_chk <- nca_res |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast") |>
  inner_join(distinct(nca_in, id, cl, cl_taz), by = "id") |>
  mutate(
    expected = ifelse(analyte == "Piperacillin", PIP_MGKG * 11 / cl, TAZ_MGKG * 11 / cl_taz),
    ratio = PPORRES / expected
  )

# Same drawn parameters on both sides; the only difference is trapezoidal
# error on a 0.05-h grid, so a tight bound is appropriate.
stopifnot(abs(median(auc_chk$ratio) - 1) < 0.02)
```

# Typical concentration profiles

```{r typical, fig.height = 4}
# One single-subject solve per regimen: a typical-value (zeroRe) solve of
# several subjects at once warns that it has no omega.
mod_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)
solve_typical <- function(reg) {
  subj <- data.frame(id = 1L, WT = 11, AGE = 2, CRCL = 120, regimen = reg)
  rxode2::rxSolve(mod_typ,
    events = make_events(subj, N_DOSES, SS_GRID),
    useLinCmt = FALSE, returnType = "data.frame"
  ) |>
    mutate(regimen = reg)
}
typ <- bind_rows(lapply(regimens, solve_typical)) |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  transmute(regimen, tad = time - 90, Piperacillin = FU * Cc, Tazobactam = FU * Cc_taz) |>
  pivot_longer(c(Piperacillin, Tazobactam), names_to = "analyte", values_to = "fconc")

ggplot(typ, aes(tad, fconc, colour = regimen)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~analyte, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    x = "Time after dose at steady state (h)", y = "Unbound concentration (mg/L)",
    colour = NULL, caption = "Typical 2-year-old, 11 kg, eGFR 120; 100/12.5 mg/kg every 6 h."
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **eGFR exponent on piperacillin clearance (erratum).** The Results display
  equation prints `(eGFR/117.9)^0.76`, while Table 2 reports 0.65 with RSE
  17.4% and a bootstrap median of 0.65 (95% CI 0.46-0.84). The model uses the
  Table 2 value. The table is internally consistent (the bootstrap CI is
  centred on 0.65, and 0.65 x 17.4% matches its width), and the closed-form
  continuous-infusion check above reproduces Figure 3 better with 0.65 than
  with 0.76. The tazobactam exponent (0.69) and both age exponents agree
  between the equations and the table.
* **Residual error form.** The paper reports a "combined constant-proportional"
  error model for piperacillin but not which Monolix form. The model uses
  Monolix's default `combined1` form, SD = a + b * f. Residual error does not
  enter any of the target-attainment checks in this article.
* **Tazobactam-limited combined PTA.** In Figure 3 the piperacillin-alone PTA
  is reproduced closely in every panel. Where the combined PTA is limited by
  tazobactam (the plateau at low MICs for the 0.5-h and 3-h infusions), the
  simulation here runs about 3-7 percentage points above the published values
  (checked with 2,000 subjects per arm, which removes most Monte Carlo
  error). The paper does not give the time grid or the exact inequality used
  to score 85% fT > 2 mg/L, and a small difference in either would explain an
  offset of this size; no parameter was changed to close it.
* **Trough concentrations in the VPC.** The simulated median at 6 h after the
  dose is about half the observed median read from Figure 2 for both drugs,
  while the 1-, 2- and 4-h medians agree within about 30%. The trough depends
  on the elimination rate, which here depends on an assumed covariate mix:
  the virtual cohort draws eGFR independently of age, and the study's
  individual weights, ages and eGFR values are not published. The Figure 2
  trough bin also holds the pre-dose samples, whose time since the previous
  dose is not reported. The Figure 3 check, which fixes the covariates, is
  the sharper test of the model.
* **Reference values.** The covariate references 117.9 mL/min/1.73 m^2 (eGFR)
  and 1.8 years (age) are those printed in the display equations. Table 1
  gives the cohort median eGFR as 120.5 among the 29 patients with an eGFR;
  the paper does not say how 117.9 was derived.
* **Steady state.** The study sampled around one dose of an ongoing regimen,
  and the paper does not report how many doses preceded sampling. The
  simulations here assume steady state, which the trough concentrations in
  Figure 2 support.
* **Target-attainment window.** The paper does not state which interval its
  Monte Carlo PTA was scored over; the steady-state interval is used here.
  Concentrations are the individual predictions without residual error.
* **Virtual cohort.** The weight-for-age relation comes from external WHO
  reference data and the eGFR spread is assumed, so the VPC comparison is
  approximate. The observed medians were read from Figure 2.
* **Figures S3-S5.** The supplementary PTA figures for the 0.5- and 8-year-old
  scenarios and the age-weight grid are not replicated; Figure 3 already tests
  every parameter in the model.
* **Covariates screened but not retained** (PELOD-2, albumin, serum creatinine,
  mechanical ventilation, vasopressor/inotrope use) are listed in the model's
  `covariatesDataExcluded` metadata.
